answer: Recursive ZK-STARK commitments anchored at a single vertex compress the network history into a verifiable proof, while sequential VDFs introduce a ferrous delay to bind the candidate. By demonstrating that cloning an identity utilizing copper accumulation hashing is information-theoretically unforgeable, these primitives ensure the protocol cannot be spoofed, as any adversary attempting to bypass the chain must resolve the sequential function at every stage to generate a valid proof chain across the network.
